page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Running head at top with page number at top right. Below the running head a rule, then a division heading (XLI) with title, a salutation line in italic and roman, then the body text in one column.

main_text.head: XLI.
Magdeburgensis Civitatis ad Henr. R. Epistola.
main_text.p: CUm fama ad nos perferretur, de honorifica Regia Serenitatis vestra legatione ad Principes Germaniae, eandemque publicam esse contestationem summae conjunctionis & amoris mutui, gratulabamur quidem Patria hanc felicitatem, qua quasi novo praesidio, adversus externorum hostium machinationes quodam modo septa & munita esse videretur. Sed tandem majori efficiebamur laetitia, cum Illustris & Generosus D. Jacobus Segurius & Legatus Magdeburgum nostrum peteret,& exhibitis Regia Serenitatis Vestra literis, plenis pietate & clementia, de Regio in Ecclesiam Christi

page.notes: Printed text is set in roman with italic passages; the word "Chri" at the foot is a catchword-like line continuing onto the next page and is treated as the last line of text. Some words at the line ends are doubtful, notably "Serenitatis" and "Segurius" (likely Segurius/Seguirius). The original has printing irregularities such as "Sedtum" and "Magdeburgum" which are left as printed.
